hypothesis: Canonical, finite-count unconditional reductions over already admitted acyclic producer CFGs can reuse bounded chunk scheduling when full-trip scratch exceeds the ceiling. Remove only (L.getNumBlocks()!=1 && !ParticipationArm) from chunk admission. This includes latch updates after one, serial or nested diamonds and the previously recognized single-diamond header updates. No recurrence, call/effect, affine-control or participation recognition is broadened; no new profitability model or original-loop vectorizability prerequisite is added.
semantics: The unchanged branch-only DAG proof removes the latch backedge/exit, admits no other external successors and processes all loop blocks from the header: the latch is the only sink and every entered iteration reaches it exactly once. For an unconditional recurrence, valid original SSA makes the contribution dominate its update. Existing recognition places that update in the latch or in an admitted diamond header; the header dominates the latch. Thus the contribution dominates the new latch scratch store. Exact use-edge closure excludes feedback from every moved accumulator or result into producer conditions, retained state, contributions or memory addresses. Every original producer branch, merge, guarded load/division/helper and original-memory operation stays in its original block/order. Chunking still requires a zero-start unit-step canonical IV with next-IV equality control in the admitted operand order, equality taking the exiting edge, and a finite representable count proof. Other affine/relational/reversed-equality controls retain full-trip-only admission. For an entered chunk, 0<=base<N and K=min(N-base,C)>0. The local ordinal resets to zero on every producer entry; exactly one latch visit increments it per original global iteration. Inductively i=0..K-1, so every scratch index is below K<=C; exit occurs at exactly K completed iterations. The unconditional consumer starts at slot zero and consumes exactly K initialized contributions in original iteration order, seeded by incoming chunk accumulators. Only then does base advance by K, without wrapping, before scratch reuse. Original nonidentity seeds and FP operand order/flags are preserved. Producer-state backedges are snapshotted before mutation and simultaneously forwarded through the dedicated producer exit; current, next, contribution and IV live-outs retain separate forwarding PHIs. All producer blocks remain mapped to the original inner loop and are added to the new chunk parent; existing ancestor membership, dedicated exits, topmost SE invalidation, DT rebuild and recursive LCSSA checks are unchanged. Exact original loop starts stay on stage preheaders and IDs through repeated LV. Strict ordinary FP and explicitly enabled fission FP reordering remain separate test rows; strictfp/constrained intrinsics and unsafe calls remain rejected. No fast-math, errno or additional numerical assumptions are added. The harness must execute actual transformed scalar/vector-tail modules against exact original IR plus an independent C traversal. New probes check actual branch edges and mixed-size scratch addresses/values per iteration, simultaneous incoming/final state, exact counts and actual vector/tail visits across boundaries.
costs: Production change: one admission-conjunct removal plus proof comments; no new analysis, CFG machinery, guards, memory accesses, streams or state arrays. Reuse the existing checked padded-capacity search (at most 64 steps over unique streams), entry allocations, min/remainder controller, local ordinal, scalar producer and ordinary-LV consumer. Storage is bounded independently of total runtime trips. New shared i32 plus double examples reserve alignTo(4*C,8)+8*C bytes: C=1/8/9/16/65 uses 16/96/112/192/784 bytes. Ceiling15 rejects a complete slot; ceiling111 fits C=8/B=96, ceiling112 fits C=9/B=112. The i32 stream feeds two sums with a single store/load stream. Logical traffic per completed original iteration is 12 bytes stored plus 12 loaded (24 bytes total), with no original input rereads, duplicated producer instructions or contribution recomputation. Three retained state carries and three reduction carries are reused. Original branch guards remain; canonical scheduling adds its existing per-chunk remaining<count select, producer latch/consumer latch and chunk continuation tests. No alias/versioning guards or compact empty-stream test is added for unconditional reductions. Code/analysis complexity remains the existing linear acyclic/effect/use/export analyses, LoopInfo membership over producer blocks and bounded capacity search. Validation adds four small original IR functions, extends the existing state certificate with original-block/latch awareness, adds two fixture-local branch/store probe hooks and one extra matrix. Validation-only input rereads/reference computations/probes are not compiler-generated traffic. Register pressure, stack-frame placement, spills, RVV execution, measured traffic and speedup are unmeasured.
limitations: No compiler, build, test runner, try.sh, module verifier, host/RVV code generation or numerical execution was invoked by this worker. All candidate outcomes remain pending harness validation. Only source/immutable-record/diff review, Python AST parsing and whitespace inspection were performed. Chunking remains canonical-only, with finite representable bounds and checked padded/pointer sizing. No new recurrence shapes, multiple participation sites, mixed participation, producer writes, unsafe effects, early-exit/cyclic CFGs, constrained/strict FP or accumulator feedback are admitted. New numerical cases have finite double data including signed zero/cancellation and arbitrary i32 bits; inherited exceptional-FP, poison, alias, enclosing-loop, dispatch and compact cases remain mandatory. The four new shapes are top-level producer CFGs; enclosing-loop and compact machinery retain inherited execution/analysis coverage. New rows do not independently claim every alias or exceptional-FP combination. EVL is uninstrumented RVV machine verification only; scalar/vector-tail execution uses fixed-vscale host adaptation, not RVV target execution. C=1 and vector widths above capacity are explicit scalar boundaries. No d2 integration is included (t000067 owns integration). Immutable accepted-head evidence has no exact-target scalar-scratch-limit rejection, so unchanged primary coverage is expected; four regression shapes demonstrate potential generality only after independent acceptance. No coverage or speedup increase is claimed.
